There are currently 55 colleges and universities, defined as accredited, degree-granting, postsecondary institutions, in the state of <Maryland>.

The state's public universities are part of the [University System of Maryland](University_System_of_Maryland "University System of Maryland"), with the exception of [United States Naval Academy](United_States_Naval_Academy "United States Naval Academy"), [St. Mary's College of Maryland](St._Mary's_College_of_Maryland "St. Mary's College of Maryland") and [Morgan State University](Morgan_State_University "Morgan State University"), which are public but are not part of the university system.[[1]](List_of_colleges_and_universities_in_Maryland#cite_note-1) The characteristics of each institution varies from small, intimate, liberal arts colleges such as [Washington College](Washington_College "Washington College") and [McDaniel College](McDaniel_College "McDaniel College") to large, public, research universities such as the [University of Maryland, College Park](University_of_Maryland%2C_College_Park "University of Maryland, College Park"). New Jersey was the only British colony to permit the establishment of two [colleges in the colonial period](Colonial_Colleges "Colonial Colleges"). [Princeton University](Princeton_University "Princeton University"), chartered in 1746 as the *College of New Jersey*, and [Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey](Rutgers_University "Rutgers University"), chartered on November 10, 1766, as *Queen's College*, were two of nine colleges founded before the American Revolution.[[3]](List_of_colleges_and_universities_in_New_Jersey#cite_note-StoeckelColonialColleges-3)[[4]](List_of_colleges_and_universities_in_New_Jersey#cite_note-4)[[5]](List_of_colleges_and_universities_in_New_Jersey#cite_note-McCormickRutgers-5): passim. The **California Community Colleges** is a postsecondary education system in the [U.S. state](U.S._state "U.S. state") of <California>.[[1]](California_Community_Colleges#cite_note-Section70900-1) Despite its plural name, the system is consistently referred to in California law as a singular entity.[[1]](California_Community_Colleges#cite_note-Section70900-1) The [system](University_system "University system") includes the Board of Governors of the California Community Colleges and 73 community college districts. The districts currently operate 116 accredited colleges. The California Community Colleges is the [largest system](List_of_largest_universities_and_university_networks_by_enrollment "List of largest universities and university networks by enrollment") of [higher education](Higher_education "Higher education") in the United States, and third largest system of higher education in the world, serving more than 1.8 million students.[[2]](California_Community_Colleges#cite_note-2)

Like the two other systems, the CCCS is headed by an executive officer and a governing board. The 17-member Board of Governors (BOG) sets direction for the system and is in turn appointed by the [California Governor](California_Governor "California Governor"). The board appoints the Chancellor, who is the chief executive officer of the system. Locally elected Boards of Trustees work on the district level with Presidents who run the individual college campuses.[[3]](California_Community_Colleges#cite_note-3)
